Mai (ML Eng): Quick heads-up — I brought up lyra-v2 (q5) on staging for multilingual evals and we're seeing two weird things: (1) Korean+Hanja bracket/order flips on detok, (2) Arabic RTL bracket mirroring on longer contexts. Anyone seen patterns like this?
Jihoon (ML Eng): I saw something similar yesterday during a smoke run. Small example below: then detok outputs swapped bracket order. Looks like tokenization/detok ordering rather than generation.
Jihoon (ML Eng) (code): ```before: 서울[漢]
after:  서울]漢[```
Sophie (NLP Evals): Can you paste the exact eval run id + sample prompt? Also which quant config did you use (q5 vs int8)?
Mai (ML Eng): run id: lyra-v2-onboard-2026-03-21-07. Quant: q5 post-training symmetric per-channel (we tried int8 earlier but baseline was q5). Sample prompt: "Translate: 서울[漢] 의 역사" -> model detok gave the bracket-flip in the korean->en run.
Marco (Serving): My first guess is detok + KV-cache prefix merging for mixed-script contexts — the detokenizer might be reordering grapheme clusters when intermediate caches are applied. We had a similar symptom on Veridian where prefix-cached segments got reflowed.
Kartik (Quant): Also check whether we applied per-tensor vs per-channel scales for embedding tables. Mixed-script embeddings can alias under aggressive quantization and cause token boundaries to shift slightly, which cascades to detok ordering.
Jihoon (ML Eng): Quick repro: disabled prefix cache on the staging node and the tiny bracket flip disappeared for the short sample. For the Arabic case it's still there.
Sophie (NLP Evals): Arabic example? Is it mirror of brackets like '(' vs ')' or directionality of paired punctuation?
Mai (ML Eng): Arabic sample: prompt with an English bracketed clause inside Arabic context; output mirrored the bracket orientation when the response length exceeded ~120 tokens. Small snippet: ```input: العربية (note: [important])
output: العربية )note: ]important[``` — looks like bidi reflow at detok time.
Marco (Serving): That suggests the bidi reordering is happening in the final detokenize pass (maybe we call an ICU function after joining subtokens). If prefix caching affects position metadata, the ICU step can mis-handle embedding of LTR segments inside RTL contexts.
Sophie (NLP Evals): We'll run targeted evals: zh->en, ko->en, ar->en with controlled context lengths and with/without prefix cache. I'll produce BLEU and chrF diffs + a tiny detok diff utility to show token boundary shifts.
eval-bot: automated eval finished for run lyra-v2-onboard-2026-03-21-07: zh->en BLEU delta -0.9, ko->en BLEU delta -0.6, ar->en BLEU delta -1.8 (q5 vs fp16 baseline). Full logs: https://ci/internal/evals/lyra-v2/2026-03-21-07
Kartik (Quant): Can we also try switching to the older int8 per-channel config we used on aurora-lites? If quantization is nudging token IDs, detok will amplify it.
Mai (ML Eng): I'll spin a small A/B: (A) q5 + prefix-cache-on, (B) q5 + prefix-cache-off, (C) int8-per-channel + prefix-cache-on. Run will include targeted detok diffs and the bidi bracket checker Sophie mentioned. ETA ~2 hrs.
Sophie (NLP Evals): I'll add per-locale char-level diffs and a small script to highlight bracket-pair flips and mirrored punctuation. Putting the script in the eval job so results are attached to run.
Marco (Serving): If disabling prefix cache fixes Korean but not Arabic, we should isolate detok ordering code paths and add reproducible unit tests for mixed-orientation pairs. I can add a small runner that calls detok with position metadata and dumps reorder ops.
Jihoon (ML Eng): FYI I reproduced a bracket-order flip locally with a minimized prompt and posted the exact bytes in the repro gist: https://internal.gists/jihoon/lyra-bracket-repro (short).
Mai (ML Eng): Thanks — will update the run with that gist and post preliminary numbers. If anyone is blocked, ping me; I'm on-call this evening. :thumbsup:
Sophie (NLP Evals): If we see BLEU delta concentrated on Arabic, might be a detok-bidi vs tokenizer canonicalization mismatch. Will try normalizing via NFKC + ICU BIDI before detok and see.
Kartik (Quant): Also flagging: if we switch quant configs, please tag the eval run metadata with quant checksum and kernel version — we had stealthy behavior changes after kernel patch 2.14.
Mai (ML Eng): noted. Action items: 1) run A/B (Mai), 2) detok reorder unit runner (Marco), 3) per-locale diff + bracket/mirror checker (Sophie), 4) try int8 variant (Kartik). I'll post results in this thread when done.
Marco (Serving): I'll try to reproduce the Arabic mirror with a forced long context; will report.
Jihoon (ML Eng): Thanks — if we need to hotfix, consider enabling fallback to fp16 detok on rtl locales while we triage.
Mai (ML Eng): Agreed. Closing loop soon.
